references.text: The expression 'no one shall sharpen their tongue' against the children of Israel is also used here, where God protects Israel during the plague of the Exodus, showing that no enemy can harm them.
The five kings hid in the cave at Makkedah, which is the same place the people returned to in peace.
Joshua captured Makkedah on the same day, which was the camp the people returned to after the victory.
The people returned to the camp after a mission, just as the spies returned after rescuing Rahab.
The Israelites returned from battle without losing a single man, showing God's protection in war.
The expression that not a hair shall fall to the ground is used to show complete protection, similar to the idea that no one could harm Israel.
